edges.description: Low IgG and IgM without clinical immunodeficiency have been documented in Lowry-Wood syndrome. In Roifman syndrome the corresponding defect is a transitional B-cell arrest from disturbed minor splicing of MAPK1, but that route has not been studied in Lowry-Wood syndrome.
u4atac deficiency produces ciliopathy-related phenotypes and ciliary defects, supporting the cilium arm of the RNU4ATAC mechanism.
edges.limitations: Transient, dose-dependent morpholino knockdown rather than a patient genotype, read out in embryos. The model is not specific to Lowry-Wood syndrome: the patient variants tested for rescue came from other RNU4ATAC phenotypes, and the fish phenotypes (body axis curvature, pronephric cysts, otolith defects) are not the epiphyseal dysplasia that defines Lowry-Wood syndrome.

nodes.description: RNU4ATAC (2q14.2) is a non-protein-coding gene for U4atac snRNA. Lowry-Wood syndrome arises from biallelic variants that impair, but do not abolish, U4atac function. Compared with MOPD I, whose variants concentrate in the 5' stem-loop needed for U4atac/U6atac.U5 tri-snRNP formation, the variants reported in Lowry-Wood syndrome are dispersed across the RNA and affect less conserved nucleotides, which fits its milder phenotype. The correlation is imperfect: the same alleles (for example n.46G>A and n.111G>A) recur across all three named RNU4ATAC phenotypes.

nodes.description: U4atac base-pairs with U6atac and is required to excise U12-type (minor) introns, present in roughly 750 human genes. In peripheral blood mononuclear cells from an adult with Lowry-Wood syndrome, minor intron retention was markedly elevated over his heterozygous father and healthy controls, and alternative splicing around minor introns was increased, so the splicing lesion has been measured directly in this phenotype rather than only inferred from MOPD I and Roifman syndrome.

nodes.description: Cilium assembly is over-represented among minor-intron-containing genes, and U4atac deficiency alters primary cilium function in patient fibroblasts and causes ciliopathy-related traits in a u4atac zebrafish model. This is the proposed route from the splicing lesion to the skeletal, retinal and brain features of the RNU4ATAC spectrum. It was shown across RNU4ATAC patients, not specifically in Lowry-Wood syndrome, and the steps from cilium dysfunction to epiphyseal dysplasia or microcephaly have not been demonstrated, so the edges below are marked as indirect.
